focus: Composer design surface inventory and rendered-board audit across all seven diagram types
noveltyJustification: First pass over the packet: every finding is new evidence from composer constants, packet references, or seven rendered boards viewed directly.
keyQuestions: What does the sk-create-figjam composer's design surface control today — palette, type scale, grid, zones, shapes, connectors, key, title block and source line — and where is each value set in compose-board.js and the packet references?

How well do the nine rendered boards in assets/screenshots hold up as visual design — first-glance hierarchy, alignment and spacing rhythm, type scale and weight, colour harmony and contrast, connector routing and label legibility, zone tints, the key, and density?
Where do the seven diagram types diverge in colour, zones and layout, which divergences are deliberate per-type identity and which are inconsistencies to unify?

What do the current boards already do well that must be preserved, and how should the quality rubric and board scorecard check a board against a design spec?

ruledOut: Zone-tint hue as the carrier of grouping — tints are near-white by design and grouping is carried by spacing, border and label
Parametrising the connector port-pricing solver in a spec file — label legibility is algorithmic, not a token

label: All visual values live in compose-board.js's constants block (SHAPE pairs, TINT+TINT_CYCLE, ~30 KINDS, TYPE scale, gap constants) — one file is the entire theme surface and the natural spec-extraction target
Colour-by-kind is already enforced semantically: kind fixes shape+colour so a colour means the same on every board; confirmed identical across all seven rendered types
The pink accent (8px outline / 4px message, 25.0 weight×contrast vs 12.6 next) lands the first glance on every board viewed — the accent system works and must be preserved
Palette is FigJam-native swatch pairs with measured contrast and self-test enforcement; custom hexes would break picker-recolourability, so a spec must stay pair-shaped
Sequence is the weakest board (19/22): fixed ROW=72 makes a tall sparse column, duplicated head/foot labels double weight, self-message loops cramped at SELF_DROP=40
Gantt planned bars are white with a thin gray stroke — they read as unfilled outlines; with only planned/crit/milestone present the chart is visually hollow except the accent bar

Zone tints are near-white and barely separate at overview; grouping is carried by the 48px gap, border and 24px zone label, not hue — six-cycle tints on the architecture board are only just distinguishable
Connector legibility is algorithmic — a port-pricing solver with restarts and pair-sweeps owns routing and labels, not cosmetic constants; a spec file must not parametrise it
The key is generated from the marks the board actually uses — 'names every mark and nothing else' by construction; spec may restyle samples but never membership
Board furniture is identical across all seven types (64-Bold title, 28 subtitle, gray Key section, 16px source line, white board section) — the strongest consistency asset
Type scale is one Inter ramp (64/28/24/20/16, 14-16 fields) with weight doing hierarchy work, constant across all seven screenshots
Spacing has two layers: judgment bands (60-92/200-400/1000+) for placed content vs composer fixed steps (80/136/48/96/80/64) — only the composer steps are tokenisable
ER is the chromatically flattest type: all-white entity cards with hierarchy resting on bold card titles, PK/FK fields and the accent alone — deliberate but lowest colour information
The packet explicitly refuses skinning today ('brand palette would turn every swatch into a custom colour'); adopting a spec file reverses a recorded decision and must keep pair-shaped values

Per-type divergences are deliberate identity (sequence pins and foot labels, gantt grid rules and section bands, state ringed finals and composite zones, architecture lane order) — types differ in vocabulary, not furniture or palette grammar
